s0301.literal: In the third year of Tianjia he died, aged forty-one.
s0301.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 he died, aged forty-one.

s0302.literal: The historian says: Du Sengming and Zhou Wenyu alike raised achievement and stood with the rising fortune; with Fan, Mu, Han, and Peng they may well be classed together.
s0302.idiomatic: The historian says: Du Sengming and Zhou Wenyu built their achievements in a rising age; they may be classed with Fan, Mu, Han, and Peng.

s0303.literal: Hou Andu's disposition differed from those of his time, his power exceeding days past; to this he added violence, and to that wantonness—if one says he was not a rebel, why should he have escaped destruction!
s0303.idiomatic: Hou Andu's temper differed from his peers and his power exceeded earlier days; add violence and wantonness—if he was no traitor, why escape ruin?

s0304.literal: In olden Han Gaozu made minced meat a gift; in Song Emperor Wu dragged [a man] from his seat at the right—there was good reason for each.
s0304.idiomatic: Han Gaozu made minced meat a gift; Song's Emperor Wu dragged a man from his seat—each had its reason.

s0307.literal: [ordered] Sengming as vanguard—changed according to the Biography of Du Sengming in the History of the Southern Dynasties and Comprehensive Mirror 345.
s0307.idiomatic: [ordered] Sengming as vanguard—emended per the Southern History biography of Du Sengming and Comprehensive Mirror 345.

s0311.literal: Later Supervisor of the Province Wang Li made Wenyu [long-stream]
s0311.idiomatic: Later provincial supervisor Wang Li made Wenyu [long-stream]

s0314.literal: Note: Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories says: "Guangzhou has no Long-stream county; the Southern History lacks the character ling—it is probably a spurious addition.
s0314.idiomatic: Note: Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories says: "Guangzhou has no Long-stream county; the Southern History lacks ling—it is probably spurious.

s0315.literal: A directorate has a long-stream aide; when aide is not written it is abbreviated text; later men wrongly added the character ling."
s0315.idiomatic: A directorate has a long-stream aide; omitting aide is abbreviation; later men wrongly added ling."

s0316.literal: The Founder because Hou Tian held
s0316.idiomatic: The Founder because Hou Tian held

s0318.literal: [Jiang] Province—changed according to the Biography of Zhou Wenyu in the Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror 345 and 395 upper.
s0318.idiomatic: [Jiang] Province—emended per the Southern History biography of Zhou Wenyu and Comprehensive Mirror 345 and 395 upper.

s0319.literal: Note: Qian Daxin's Examination of the Twenty-two Histories says "Wen Province" is probably a corruption for "Jiang Province."
s0319.idiomatic: Note: Qian Daxin says "Wen Province" is probably a corruption for Jiang Province.

s0320.literal: Still removed [him] as Director-General of all military affairs in Southern Yuzhou
s0320.idiomatic: Still removed [him] as director-general of all military affairs in Southern Yuzhou

s0322.literal: affairs, General of Martial Prestige, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou—the character zhi is spurious; deleted according to all editions.
s0322.idiomatic: affairs, general of martial prestige, and Southern Yuzhou inspector—the character zhi is spurious; deleted per all editions.

s0323.literal: The two characters "affairs martial" were originally lacunae in the ink; supplied according to all editions.
s0323.idiomatic: The two characters affairs martial were lacunae in the ink; supplied per all editions.

s0324.literal: Note: "General of Martial Prestige" in Comprehensive Mirror 345 and 395 upper both read "General of Stern Prestige."
s0324.idiomatic: Note: general of martial prestige in Comprehensive Mirror 345 and 395 upper both read general of stern prestige.

s0325.literal: Troops did not meet the wind—note: the Southern History reads "arrows" for "troops."
s0325.idiomatic: On "troops did not meet the wind": the Southern History reads arrows for troops.

s0326.literal: Galloping forward—the character "gallop" was originally a lacuna in the ink; supplied according to Comprehensive Mirror 345 and 395 upper.
s0326.idiomatic: On "galloping forward": gallop was a lacuna in the ink; supplied per Comprehensive Mirror 345 and 395 upper.

s0327.literal: Note: the character "gallop" is missing in all editions.
s0327.idiomatic: Note: gallop is missing in all editions.

s0328.literal: Sihui and the rest moved camp to Mofu Mountain—the character "mountain" was originally a lacuna in the ink; supplied according to all editions.
s0328.idiomatic: On "Sihui and the rest moved camp to Mofu Mountain": mountain was a lacuna in the ink; supplied per all editions.

s0329.literal: At that time the cave lord of Xinwu, Yu Xiaoxiang,
s0329.idiomatic: At that time the cave lord of Xinwu, Yu Xiaoxiang,

s0331.literal: [raised] troops to answer Bo—changed according to all editions.
s0331.idiomatic: [raised] troops to answer Bo—emended per all editions.

s0332.literal: at Shanglao—the character "at" was originally a lacuna in the ink; supplied according to all editions.
s0332.idiomatic: On "at Shanglao": at was a lacuna in the ink; supplied per all editions.

s0333.literal: Wenyu sent General of Stern Prestige Zhou Tiewu—"Zhou Tiewu" in the Hall edition reads "Zhou Tiehu."
s0333.idiomatic: On "Wenyu sent general of stern prestige Zhou Tiewu": the Hall edition reads Zhou Tiehu for Zhou Tiewu.

s0334.literal: Note: because Ssu-chien avoided Tang taboo, all characters "hu" were changed to "wu"; those reading "hu" are later reversals.
s0334.idiomatic: Note: because Ssu-chien avoided Tang taboo, hu was changed to wu; hu readings are later reversals.

s0335.literal: Father Wenhan—note: the Southern History lacks the character "wen."
s0335.idiomatic: On "father Wenhan": the Southern History lacks wen.

s0336.literal: Xu Sihui and the rest again entered Danyang—the character "si" was originally a lacuna in the ink; supplied according to all editions.
s0336.idiomatic: On "Xu Sihui and the rest again entered Danyang": si was a lacuna in the ink; supplied per all editions.

s0337.literal: The Qi army was greatly defeated—the character "great" was originally corrupt as "enter"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
s0337.idiomatic: On "the Qi army was greatly defeated": great was miswritten enter; all editions are correct; now emended.

s0338.literal: Lin's general Pan Chun'ai shot at the government army from afar in the city—"Pan Chun'ai" in the Southern History reads "Pan Chun."
s0338.idiomatic: On "Lin's general Pan Chun'ai shot at the government army from the city": the Southern History reads Pan Chun for Pan Chun'ai.

s0344.literal: Note: the Treatise on the Sui also reads "Lu."
s0344.idiomatic: Note: the Treatise on the Sui also reads Lu.

s0347.literal: [to attack] Yi—Hall edition textual verification by Sun Renlong says: "According to the passage above, Liu Yi set palisades to resist the royal army; then this character shou is probably a corruption for gong attack."
s0347.idiomatic: On "[to attack] Yi": Hall edition verification by Sun Renlong says that since Liu Yi set palisades above, shou here is probably a corruption for attack.

s0348.literal: Note: Comprehensive Mirror 216 correctly reads "attack"; now changed accordingly.
s0348.idiomatic: Note: Comprehensive Mirror 216 reads attack; now emended accordingly.

s0350.literal: [Officials] and people came to court with a memorial requesting a stele—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror 803.
s0350.idiomatic: On "[officials] and people petitioned for a stele": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, Southern History, and Comprehensive Mirror 803.

s0354.literal: Note: Chu Jie has a biography in this book.
s0354.idiomatic: Note: Chu Jie has a biography in this book.

s0355.literal: Liu Shan—note: the Southern History reads shan as "shan" (coral).
s0355.idiomatic: On "Liu Shan": the Southern History reads shan as coral shan.

s0357.literal: [secretly] burying and digging up—changed according to the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.
s0357.idiomatic: On "[secretly] burying and digging up": emended per the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.

s0358.literal: Note: the language is from the Biography of the Cruel Official Wang Wenshu in the Records of the Grand Historian, "in youth he secretly buried loot and did evil."
s0358.idiomatic: Note: the phrase comes from the Grand Historian biography of the cruel official Wang Wenshu: "in youth he secretly buried loot and did evil."
